roles: Technical Program and Project Manager, AI Delivery
seat: Build a lightweight collaborative document editor inspired by Google Docs, demonstrating document creation/editing, file upload, sharing, persistence, and engineering quality within a 4-6 hour timebox, showing product judgment and full-stack execution.
core_skill: Turning an open-ended product prompt into a coherent, shippable full-stack slice with deliberate prioritization under time pressure.

anchors.5: Creates, renames, edits, saves, and reopens documents; supports all five rich-text formats (bold, italic, underline, headings/text size, bulleted/numbered lists); editing flow feels usable and coherent per assessment's 'usable and coherent' bar.
anchors.3: Implements core CRUD for documents and at least three of five rich-text formats; editing works but has noticeable gaps (e.g., missing list support or heading levels don't persist).
anchors.1: Only plain-text editing or document CRUD is broken; rich-text formatting largely absent or non-functional.

anchors.5: Uploads at least one file type (.txt, .md, or .docx) and converts it into a new editable document or attaches it to a document; UI clearly states supported types per 'If you limit supported file types, state that clearly in the UI and README'.
anchors.3: Uploads files but conversion to editable document is partial (e.g., .txt works but .md/.docx not handled) or attachment association is missing; supported types documented.
anchors.1: File upload missing or non-functional; no supported-type disclosure in UI/README.

anchors.5: Implements document owner, a way to grant another user access, and a visible distinction between owned and shared documents; works with seeded/mocked auth per 'You may simulate users with seeded accounts, mocked auth, or a lightweight login flow'.
anchors.3: Basic sharing exists (e.g., grant access) but owned vs shared distinction is missing or sharing logic has gaps (e.g., no owner concept, or shared users cannot open).
anchors.1: Sharing not implemented or purely stubbed; no multi-user demonstration possible.

anchors.5: Documents survive refresh, formatting/structure preserved (rich-text round-trips), and shared access behavior demonstrable end-to-end; uses practical storage (SQLite, Postgres, Supabase, or documented file-based store).
anchors.3: Documents persist but formatting loss on reload (e.g., HTML/JSON not fully round-tripped) or shared access not fully verifiable after refresh.
anchors.1: No persistence or data lost on refresh; storage approach undocumented.

anchors.5: Includes all five minimums: clear setup/run instructions, working deployment reviewers can access, basic validation/error handling, at least one meaningful automated test, and a short architecture note explaining prioritization and why.
anchors.3: Missing one or two of the five minimums (e.g., no automated test or architecture note incomplete); deployment works but setup instructions unclear.
anchors.1: Missing three or more minimums; no deployment link or project cannot be run locally.

anchors.5: AI workflow note identifies specific tools, where AI materially sped up work, what AI-generated output was changed/rejected, and how correctness/UX/reliability were verified; demonstrates judgment not volume.
anchors.3: Note covers tools and speedups but lacks concrete examples of changed/rejected output or verification steps; reads like a log not a judgment.
anchors.1: No AI workflow note, or generic boilerplate without specifics to this project.

anchors.5: All deliverables present (README.md, architecture note, AI note, SUBMISSION.md, live URL, video URL, screenshots/GIF) per 'Submit one Google Drive folder containing:'; video 3-5 min covers main flow, working end-to-end, deprioritized items, key decisions, AI support; SUBMISSION.md lists exactly what's included; any partial features clearly state what works, what's incomplete, next steps.
anchors.3: Most deliverables present but one missing (e.g., no video or SUBMISSION.md incomplete); video exceeds 5 min or omits required sections; partial features not clearly documented.
anchors.1: Multiple missing deliverables; no video; SUBMISSION.md absent; incomplete features undocumented.

anchors.5: Architecture note and video explicitly map each scope cut to a timebox tradeoff, explain why the remaining slice is coherent, and show the cut was intentional not accidental; deprioritized items listed with 'what you would build next with another 2-4 hours'.
anchors.3: Some scope cuts explained but rationale is thin or post-hoc; deprioritized list exists but doesn't connect to the 4-6 hour constraint.
anchors.1: No scope cuts acknowledged, or cuts appear accidental (broken features passed as complete); no 'what you would build next' section.

auto_fails: No live deployment URL provided (reviewers cannot test the product)
No Google Drive folder with source code (cannot review implementation)
Sharing flow completely absent (core requirement Task 3)
Document editing is plain-text only with no rich-text formatting (fails Task 1 core)
No persistence - documents lost on refresh (fails Task 4)
AI workflow note missing entirely (explicit requirement)
red_flags: Deployment requires paid service or reviewer payment (violates 'Do not require reviewers to pay for a dependency or service')
Supported file types not disclosed in UI/README when limited
No seeded users/credentials provided for sharing demo
Architecture note missing or generic boilerplate
Automated test is trivial (e.g., only tests true === true)

tells.strong: Architecture note explicitly maps each scope cut to a timebox tradeoff and explains why the remaining slice is coherent
tells.weak: README lists features not actually implemented in the live deployment

gia.why: The assessment demands rapid synthesis of ambiguous product requirements into a coherent technical plan and clear written artifacts under time pressure.

triage.label: Live deployment URL is accessible and loads without authentication errors
Google Drive folder link provided and contains source code directory
README.md includes local setup and run instructions that work
Seeded users or test credentials provided to demonstrate owned vs shared document distinction
Editor supports at least bold, italic, and one of (heading/list/underline) per Task 1
AI workflow note (Markdown/PDF) exists and names specific tools used
